Signs Your Child Needs an Eye Checkup in Mumbai 

Children rarely complain about their vision.

Not because nothing is wrong, but because they have no reference point for what clear vision should feel like. If a child has always seen the world in a certain way, they may simply assume that is how everyone sees it.

This is why parents and caregivers play such an important role in spotting the early signs that a child may need an eye examination.

Signs worth paying attention to include:
1. Squinting when looking at distant objects or a screen
2. Sitting unusually close to the television or holding books very near the face
3. Complaints of headaches, particularly after reading or schoolwork
4. Rubbing the eyes frequently
5. Tilting the head to one side when focusing
6. A noticeable drop in concentration or academic performance

None of these signs individually confirm a vision problem, but one or more of them together suggest that a thorough eye examination is worthwhile.

From age 4 years onwards, a routine annual eye examination for kids is recommended even if no symptoms present. 

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Dadar, our specialist team conducts comprehensive eye examinations for children, tailored to their age and developmental stage.

Early attention supports healthy visual development.

Struggling with Colour Vision? Visit Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co. 

Colour vision deficiency is often discovered by chance.

A comment from a family member. A test at school. A moment of uncertainty when trying to distinguish between two colours that others seem to differentiate with ease.

For many people, it has simply always been this way, and they have never sought a formal assessment or explored what options might be available to them.

A structured colour vision assessment provides clarity. It identifies the specific type of colour vision deficiency present, its severity, and whether any supportive options such as specialist lenses may be of benefit.

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Dadar, our specialist team conducts detailed colour vision evaluations in a calm, unhurried clinical environment.

Toric Contact Lenses for Astigmatism – Available at Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co.

If you have astigmatism and have tried standard contact lenses before, you may have found that they do not provide the clarity you were hoping for.

Astigmatism occurs when the cornea or natural lens of the eye has an irregular curvature, causing light to focus at more than one point on the retina. Standard spherical contact lenses are not designed to correct this, so vision can remain blurred or distorted even when wearing them.

Toric contact lenses are specifically designed for eyes with astigmatism. These lenses have different powers in different meridians of the lens and are generally weighted to remain correctly oriented on the eye.

Other materials are available for more irregular or higher cylindrical corrections, with bespoke fits helping achieve maximum comfort and vision.

When fitted accurately, toric lenses can provide clear, stable vision throughout the day for patients with astigmatism who prefer contact lenses over spectacles.

The right fit depends on a precise contact lens assessment, fit and follow up.

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Dadar, our team conducts thorough assessments to ensure the most appropriate lens is recommended for your individual prescription and ocular health.

Early Cataract Signs – Advice from Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co. 

Cataracts develop slowly, and that is precisely what makes them easier to miss in the early stages.

The natural lens inside the eye gradually becomes cloudy over time, affecting how much light and how well it passes through to the retina. In the early stages, colours may appear slightly less vivid. Vision may seem a little hazy, particularly in bright light or at night. Contrast sensitivity may change noticeably for people with certain visual demands.

Common early signs include:
1. Increased sensitivity to glare, especially when driving at night
2. Colours appearing less bright or slightly yellowed
3. A gradual blurring of vision that does not improve with a new glasses prescription
4. Difficulty reading in low light conditions

These changes often develop so gradually that they are attributed to ageing rather than a specific condition. This is why regular specialist eye examinations are important, particularly from middle age onwards.

Are vision correction treatments like LASIK Safe? 

It is one of the most common questions we hear.

LASIK is a laser-based vision correction procedure that reshapes the cornea, the clear, front surface of the eye, to reduce or eliminate the need for glasses or contact lenses. It has been performed for decades and has an excellent, established safety profile.

Please bring any previous eye reports, your current prescription glasses, and a list of any ongoing medications you take.

A comprehensive vision test and eye exam typically take 30 to 45 minutes. If your consultation requires pupil dilation for a deeper evaluation, please plan for up to 2 hours.

We perform a complete vision test alongside refraction to check your glasses prescription. Dr. Ami Shah also conducts an eye pressure check and a detailed slit-lamp examination to evaluate both the anterior and interior health of your eyes.

With over 10 years of experience, Dr. Ami Shah provides complete care including modern laser vision correction, advanced micro-incision cataract surgery with premium lens options, and comprehensive glaucoma screenings. We also specialize in dry eye treatment and routine pediatric eye evaluations.

Eyecare tips in summer.

During Summers, a mix of heat, dust and dehydration can cause several eye issues. 
Here are some tips which can help prevent eye issues. 

1. Don’t skip sunglasses
Go for sunglasses that block 99–100% of UV rays. Prolonged UV exposure can increase the risk of conditions like cataracts and photokeratitis. 

2.Stay hydrated
Your eyes rely on proper tear production. Dehydration can worsen dryness and irritation, sometimes leading to dry eye syndrome.

3.Limit direct sun exposure
Try to avoid peak sunlight hours (roughly 11 AM–4 PM). Wearing a hat or sunglasses will protect your eyes.

4.Protect against dust and pollution
If you’re outdoors a lot, especially in windy or dusty areas, use protective eyewear. Dust can trigger allergies. 

5.Use lubricating eye drops (if needed)
Artificial tears can help keep your eyes moist, especially if you spend time in air-conditioned rooms.
